propositions: Gerrit Verified macOS wall-clock execution regressed from 15–20 minutes to 30–40 minutes; root cause is combination of test suite growth (~4.1k additional selected tests, ~91k net test lines), expensive unit test mechanics (120s timeouts, 25s real sleeps, 34k AST parses per guard call, per-xdist wiki corpus recomputation), and subprocess/APFS contention amplification under GitHub Free org limits (5 macOS concurrent jobs).

Mutation testing was added at commit e0b3fdfc8e and occurred in 5/62 subsequent successful runs; mutation was not the critical path in any run, did not explain the latency present in 57 skipped-mutation runs, and cannot account for the 14m31s pytest growth on macOS.

Seven specific test fixtures execute production-scale mechanics unnecessarily: 120s missing-field timeout, five 5s real sleeps, 34k per-guard AST parses with missing cache, per-xdist wiki corpus fills, N=3000 import event load, and production-scale socket/process timing windows.

Investigation identified dated transition from run 30723712651 (2026-08-01, 15–20m baseline) to run 31631448140 (7a1863f, 30–40m regression) with +870s pytest growth and +4.1k selected tests; no code changes were made, coverage was preserved, and remediation decomposed into seven linked tracker tickets.

Post-remediation final sample (run 31752047186, 2026-08-13) achieved 27m46s workflow wall with macOS default pytest at 22m15s; long-pole tests include wiki corpus (149.13s), bridge hourly-cadence (100–130s), editor setup (35.04s), and distributed work across 12,914 passing tests.
Existing telemetry (--durations=25 logs) was sufficient for root-cause analysis; no observability code change was required or merged.
